diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Mohammad Amin Mandani, a prisoner held in Tehran's central prison, was sentenced to death and 20 years in prison by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. His charges include cooperating with hostile states and gathering and conspiring against national security. The sentence was issued by Judge Iman Afshari.

The Yemeni government forces carried out airstrikes on areas controlled by the Houthis in Sana'a. These attacks occurred on Saturday, 11 Mehr, and smoke was seen in the city's sky. The Houthis are supported by the Islamic Republic.

The mother of Moein Abbaspour responded to Masoud Pezeshkian's claim that her son was a terrorist by questioning why the Islamic Republic's Martyrs Foundation approached their family to declare him a martyr. This reaction was seen in a video released on social media. The issue arose during Pezeshkian's trip to the United States.

Hamid Kouhsari, a 31-year-old protester, said he was shot in the leg by security forces during the December 2025 protests in Gorgan. He reported direct shooting by security forces at protesters and the killing and wounding of citizens. Kouhsari also spoke about living in hiding for eight months before leaving Iran.

The head of the Automotive Parts Manufacturers Association stated that sanctions and transportation issues have increased costs. Additionally, liquidity problems and the need for loans have risen due to inflation and price increases. He called for at least a 100% increase in loans to secure raw materials.

A group of Iranians gathered in Stockholm for the tenth consecutive month in protest. Participants held pictures of the deceased and commemorated them. They called for global attention to developments in Iran.

At the autumn conference of the European Criminal Lawyers Association in Albania, the 2026 Scott Krazby Human Rights Award was given to Nasrin Sotoudeh. The award recognizes her over two decades of work defending women's rights and fundamental rights. Nasrin Sotoudeh had previously been detained for her activities and was recently released on bail.

The Iranian national volleyball team defeated Japan 3-1 in the final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya and became the champion. This victory is the 19th gold medal for Iran's delegation in these games. The set scores were 26-28, 25-19, 21-25, and 24-26.

A group of Iranians living in Australia gathered on Saturday, 11 Mehr, in Adelaide. They expressed their support for the national revolution and Prince Reza Pahlavi. This event was recorded in videos received by Iran International.

A worker employed in the manganese mine of Vanarch in Qom province died due to the collapse of part of one of the mine's tunnels. The incident occurred in the Vanarch manganese mine. Further details have not been announced.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the Central Bank governor, described the rise in the dollar price as temporary and attributed it to American propaganda shocks. However, 36 days later, the dollar surpassed 250,000 tomans. This indicates a continued upward trend in the dollar price.

Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that for the first time since Iran began oil production, it has no oil on water this week and will have no revenue from oil sales. He attributed this situation to US military and economic actions against Iran. These measures included military conflict, blockade, and an economic expulsion operation.

Mehran Qarabaghi, a political prisoner from Behbahan, was released from Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz after completing his sentence. He was transferred to Taft city to serve a two-year exile sentence. This transfer took place on Thursday, Mehr 9.

A column of smoke and fire was seen near an Aramco facility in Riyadh on Saturday, October 3. Saudi authorities and Aramco have not commented on the incident. No group has claimed responsibility for the fire.

Ali Belali, advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, stated that the supply chain for weapons and missiles is intact and production continues without interruption. He said all missile equipment is made inside Iran and the armed forces have sufficient missile capability to continue fighting. He also claimed that the US copied Iran's Shahed 136 drone.

South Korea's under-23 football team defeated Japan 1-0 in the final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya with a goal by Um Ji-sung. They won the gold medal for the fourth consecutive time in this competition. South Korea's victory led to the players being exempted from mandatory military service.

The forced eviction of an 87-year-old woman after more than seven decades in her home in Madrid led to protests by tens of thousands. Protesters demand stronger tenant protections and a halt to evictions without alternative housing. This report was published by Sajedeh Sharifi from Iran International.

Behzad Yazdani, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Shiraz, has been detained for over 180 days without access to a lawyer or a court hearing. He was arrested on the 9th of Farvardin by the IRGC intelligence. His family has not received any judicial response regarding his case status.

Hassan Mansour, an economist, attributed the 30,000 toman increase in the dollar price within a week to capital flight, reduced trust in the rial, and government policies to cover budget deficits. He stated that the rise in currency prices makes imported goods more expensive and creates inflationary expectations. This situation encourages people and sellers to buy and price goods based on higher future rates.
Khizr Rasul Marut, a citizen of Mahabad, was arrested and transferred to Mahabad prison to serve his sentence. This occurred today. More details are provided in the full article.

Videos and images show a storm and dust rising in Qom province. Reports indicate that several power distribution feeders in the province have gone offline. This event was reported on social media and Iran International.

Around 16:30 in Qeshm, a very loud and terrifying sound of a missile launch or fighter jet passage was heard. Some reports mention a missile launch towards the strait and air defense activation. The source of this news is Vahid Online.

A video shows an Iranian citizen shouting at an Iranian athlete holding the Islamic Republic's flag during the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan. This incident occurred during the Asian Games. The citizen shouted, "This is the flag."
Several athletes, including wrestlers, died during the protests in Iran. Mehdi Rostampour spoke about these victims. Among those killed are Taha Safari, Parsa Lorestani, and Saleh Mohammadi.

The Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic announced the arrest of 31 people in Sirjan. These individuals are accused of being members of four organized street sabotage networks. They are charged with involvement in setting fire to the governor's office and damaging government buildings in December 2025 events.

Nine female political prisoners in Evin Prison have been deprived of phone calls for one month starting Saturday, October 3. Their phone cards were deactivated without explanation. Prison authorities stated this measure continues the restrictions on their visitations.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, stated in an interview with Axios that for the first time since Iran began oil exports, this week no oil will be loaded for sea transport. He also said the US has facilitated the passage of 1.1 billion barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz and that Washington is isolating Iran unprecedentedly.

The price of the US dollar in the free market surpassed 270,000 tomans for the first time, reaching about 271,000 tomans. This increase was more than 13,000 tomans over two days. The Central Bank announced plans to supply two billion dollars in cash to the market, and the judiciary is taking action against channels causing false currency pricing.

The Central Bank plans to block the accounts and payment gateways of some cryptocurrency exchanges. These restrictions are due to artificial order placements causing disruptions in the Tether market. Nighttime trading of Tether has also been halted in these exchanges.
Several missiles were launched from Qeshm around 4:35. One of the missiles hit the Moddares Public School. A piece of the missile body was found near the school.

The expulsion order of Ali Ahangark Bahani, a master's student in mechanical engineering at Shahid Beheshti University, was confirmed by the university's appeals council. The order was confirmed as is. More information is provided in the continuation of the article.

Javad Hosseini Kia described Masoud Pezeshkian's statements as a sign of weakness to the enemy and called it a strategic mistake. He said showing weakness to the enemy is like giving them an assist. He also stated that telling the truth to the people is not related to sending a signal of weakness.

Mohammad Javad Fazel Lankarani called for expanding nighttime gatherings of government supporters until the enemy is completely defeated. He stated that Iran's military forces have acquired more advanced weapons in recent months. According to him, the enemy talks and lies a lot because of Iran's increased military power.
Iranians residing in Helsinki gathered on October 3rd. They commemorated the immortal figures of Iran and the Lion and Sun Revolution. This event took place in the capital of Finland.

Trump said big news about Iran is coming. The aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt with 10,000 Marines has moved toward the Middle East to form the largest US military buildup since the 2003 Iraq occupation.
Arian Salimi won the gold medal in taekwondo. Hedi Hajimousaei took silver and Fatemeh Ahmadi won bronze. Nahid Kiani was eliminated from the competition.

Nahid Kiani in the women's taekwondo under 57 kg category won against a Kazakh opponent but lost to Lin Chen from Taiwan and was eliminated from the competition. This news was reported by Alireza Modiri.

Saipa customers protested on Saturday at the company's customer service office due to severe delays in vehicle delivery. They expressed their dissatisfaction with the situation. A video of the protest was sent to Iran International.

Atta Hosseinian, citing data from institutions like Kepler, stated that Iran's oil exports during the second naval blockade have nearly dropped to zero. The docking of tankers at Khark and Jask terminals has decreased. The best-case oil export volume is about 80,000 barrels per day.

Donald Trump announced the deployment of about 9,000 new US troops to the Middle East. Simultaneously, the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt and the amphibious group Makin Island are moving toward the region, and the number of US naval forces in the region will exceed 20,000.

Tens of thousands of students and teachers in France protested due to crowded classrooms and teacher shortages. The protests involved over 1,200 high schools, and teachers have indicated a possible strike after the 2027 budget announcement. Authorities reported the arrest of more than 5,000 people, mostly teenagers.

Roberto Piazza, head coach of Iran's national volleyball team, expressed gratitude for the support from the Iranian people after winning gold at the Nagoya Asian Games. He stated the tournament was not easy and the players aimed to do something special for Iran. Piazza also hopes to win more medals in the future and is optimistic about Iranian talents.
Benjamin Netanyahu said US pressure and siege have severely weakened the IRGC and the Islamic Republic will collapse.

Najat Bahrami, a political analyst, sees the increased US military presence and allied movements as signs of a move toward a broad conflict. He states that Trump's goal is not necessarily to overthrow the Islamic Republic but to weaken it to the point of surrender. This analysis indicates a shift in the regional political atmosphere.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, attended the government's economic coordination headquarters meeting. He described the current situation as one of the most difficult periods for the country. Rezaei also stated that the negotiation process is very serious.

The Brazil national football team defeated India 4-0 in a friendly match at Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata. Samuel Lino scored two goals in the second half, while Stau and Pedro scored in the first half. Carlo Ancelotti led the team to victory with players like Vinicius Junior and Marquinhos in the lineup.

Hamam Al-Hamami, the co-pilot of the FlyDubai flight, lived in Syria for several years and is suspected of joining a group linked to the Islamic Republic. He stated in interrogation that he intended to crash the plane into a target in Israel. Investigations involving multiple countries are ongoing to examine his possible connections and group support.

The One Million Signatures Campaign for Changing Discriminatory Laws turned twenty this September. The campaign aimed to change unequal laws and collect signatures, becoming an important experience in the Iranian women's movement. Parvin Ardalan, one of the founders, discussed the history and impact of the campaign.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said in the program "Cheshmandaz" that Iranian officials are worried about a possible US ground attack. He added that the US is reinforcing its forces in the region. Additionally, three US aircraft carriers are scheduled to be deployed in the region starting next month.

Alireza Rashidi, a 16-year-old teenager from Ashkhaneh in North Khorasan province, was arrested on Wednesday, October 8. The arrest is related to the nationwide protests of December 1404. Security forces were responsible for the arrest.

A student sent a video to Iran International asking compatriots to be the voice of Iranian students worldwide. This request aims to gain international support. The video was sent to Iran International.

A man accused of killing a 17-year-old girl in Tehran for honor motives has been sentenced to death. The sentence was issued by Branch 12 of the Tehran Criminal Court. In addition to the death penalty, other punishments have also been assigned to him.

The England national football team defeated Croatia 7-0 in the third week of the UEFA Nations League. Harry Kane and Saka each scored twice, with additional goals from Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon, and Rogers. The match was held without regular spectators, and England reached a higher level after their loss to Spain.
A few days after Trump's renewed warning about possible new attacks on Iran, Axios reported that next steps in the war were discussed in a meeting with senior US officials.

Ahead of the US midterm elections, the dispute over mail-in voting restrictions has reached the Postal Service and the Supreme Court. The Trump administration sought to change the mail-in voting process through an executive order, but the Supreme Court in September halted the implementation of new postal regulations for the upcoming elections.
Gas poisoning in a well in Bijar caused the death of one worker and injury to another. The number of injured in a building collapse incident in Zanjan has increased from one to four.
A severe storm in Qom caused a chain collision on the Qom-Kashan road. One person died and 15 others were injured in the incident. The accident occurred on Saturday, Mehr 11.

Keyhan Takahashi in volleyball and Arash Yoshida in wrestling are two Iranian-descended athletes who competed for Japan in the Nagoya Asian Games. This report was prepared by Somayeh Mehri from Iran International.

Younes Azadbar, a resident of Rasht, was summoned to Branch 15 of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of Rasht. The charges include conspiracy against internal security, propaganda against the regime, and publishing content against national security. He must appear within five days to defend himself.

Rouhollah Lak Aliabadi said that the US is trying to prepare the ground for an attack on Iran through military movements and propaganda. He added that the US wants to link the Flydubai flight incident to Iran and blame the Islamic Republic. The goal is to prepare global public opinion for an attack on Iran.

A video of the demolition of the watchtower of Rajai Shahr prison in Karaj has been released. This prison, known for human rights violations and mass executions of political prisoners, was officially closed in August 2023. The prisoners have been transferred to other prisons.

A group of Iranians marched in Stockholm on Saturday carrying the Lion and Sun flag and images of Prince Reza Pahlavi. The march was in support of political prisoners and in protest against the execution of protesters in Iran. Videos of the event were sent to Iran International.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, stated that if the Islamic Republic does not make the right choice, Donald Trump will have all necessary options regarding Iran on the table. He said preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons is a vital US interest, and Washington will do whatever is necessary. He also mentioned that Iran does not control the Strait of Hormuz and the US can maintain or change the blockade as needed.

Meysam Mehrani said Saudi Arabia targets the command centers, missile depots, and supply routes of the Houthis. He added that the Houthis attack Saudi Arabia's energy and oil infrastructure to shift its military focus from offense to defense.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the government has taken new measures to manage the special conditions. He said economic pressure has increased but the enemy's goals in the economic war have not been achieved. These remarks come as the dollar price reached 270,000 tomans and reports indicate a severe livelihood crisis.

Two members of the Islamic Republic's delegation to the UN were expelled from the US after failing to comply with the State Department's order to leave the country. The US State Department repeatedly informed the Iranian delegation that all members must immediately leave US soil. These two diplomats left the US on Friday night and Saturday morning.

Bruno Fernandes, captain of Portugal's national team, spoke about Cristiano Ronaldo in a press conference before the match against Norway. He emphasized that Ronaldo will never lose his status as the greatest symbol of the national team. Fernandes hopes the issue will end well and called for respect for all sides.

Ahmad Donyamali, the Minister of Sports and Youth, spoke about visa issues for the national team's companions at the 2026 World Cup and FIFA's performance at the World Cup. He said they should move away from the legal space of FIFA and pay attention to the problems caused by US sanctions. The Minister emphasized that despite the sanctions, Iran will continue to fight.

Ivar Farhadi stated that the US is preparing for possible conflict scenarios with the Islamic Republic by deploying a third aircraft carrier and air defense systems in Qatar and Saudi Arabia. He said the Islamic Republic has lost much of its leverage but can still increase the cost of conflict by attacking energy infrastructure and activating proxy forces.

Asieh Amini stated that women political prisoners are deprived of contact with family, visits, medicine, and books. She added that these pressures are part of the Islamic Republic's intensified punishment. The regime also uses women's gender roles to impose harsher punishments.

Rojan Ebrahimi, a 20-year-old MMA athlete from Saqez, was arrested by security forces. The intelligence agency raided her home without a judicial warrant and transferred her to an unknown location. The reason for her arrest is still unknown.

Alex Winston spoke about the deep connection between the people of Iran and Israel at the fifth Iran conference of the Nufdi Institute in Washington. He emphasized that the media should convey the voices of Iranian protesters to the world. These statements were made in an interview with Iran International.

Videos published on social media show flooding in various areas of Karaj and Alborz province after the rains on Saturday, October 3. As of the time of publication, no reports on damages or casualties have been released. Officials of the Islamic Republic have not yet provided an official report.

Morad Vaisi stated that the dollar has surpassed 270,000 tomans in Iran's currency market. He described Iran's economy as collapsing and the country on the brink of economic chaos. People are witnessing a decline in the value of their assets and purchasing power.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, announced that Iran's oil exports have been completely cut off starting this week. This is the first time in 118 years that Iran's oil exports have reached zero. Murad Vaisi mentioned this while describing the Iranian government as incompetent.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, stated that some government offices distribute meat on installment plans to their employees. He considers this a sign of worsening economic conditions in Iran. He described this situation as a stage before famine.

Bourgan Nezami stated that the sharp increase in the dollar rate in Iran is due to the pressure of war, US economic sanctions, and structural economic crises. He identified central bank policies as factors intensifying distrust and inflation expectations. He also warned that the gap between exchange and free market rates could trigger a new wave of inflation.

Mehdi Kharatian said China told Iranian officials that cooperation with Iran is risky and prefers to keep it behind the scenes. Also, China stopped sending satellite images to Iran for an attack on a US destroyer after the issue was exposed.

Reza Pahlavi sent a message to the birthday ceremony of Nika Shakarami in Frankfurt, calling her a symbol of Iranian resistance in the fight for freedom. He praised Nika's bravery and her role in the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising. He also thanked Nika's mother for opposing the Islamic Republic's narrative.

Pete Hegseth declined to disclose how many US aircraft carriers will remain in the Middle East after the arrival of the Theodore Roosevelt. He stated his duty is to provide the widest range of options to the commander-in-chief. Hegseth also mentioned that the conflict with the Islamic Republic could be resolved in various ways.

Houshang Hasan-Yari said Donald Trump's threat to Tehran to choose between an "easy path" and a "difficult path" means demanding the complete surrender of the Islamic Republic. He added that the US has strengthened its military presence in the region and kept the option of attack ready. The likelihood of conflict increases if Tehran does not accept Washington's demands, and the US goal may extend beyond the nuclear program.

Donald Trump stated that Washington will make decisions regarding the Islamic Republic and described the Iranian government as destroyed. He said the Biden administration did not act to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump also added that Iran has effectively abandoned its nuclear program and oil prices are falling.

Donald Trump said at a campaign rally in Ohio that the Islamic Republic of Iran will never acquire nuclear weapons. Referring to Kim Jong Un and North Korea's nuclear arsenal, he stressed that unlike North Korea, Iran will never obtain such weapons.

Joe Wilson, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, posted images of Hashd al-Shaabi forces walking over the American flag and accused the Iraqi government of being under the influence of the Islamic Republic. Wilson wrote on X that Hashd al-Shaabi is seen disrespecting the American flag and praising the Iranian government. He also said that Iraq should be freed from Iranian influence.

Pete Hegseth said Donald Trump has given multiple opportunities to the Islamic Republic. He added that US attacks and blockade have limited Tehran's options. Hegseth emphasized that the Islamic Republic will never acquire nuclear weapons and Washington will take necessary measures.

The Jerusalem Post news editor emphasized the need to amplify the voices of those facing repression and execution risks amid protests and media restrictions in Iran. He highlighted solidarity between the people of Iran and Israel and described the Starlink device display at the UN as symbolic. He stated efforts are being made to share the stories of victims' families and prisoners with audiences outside Iran.

Nicolas Gilani stated that Iran's central bank has lost control over the rising dollar rate. He also said the simultaneous surge in inflation and exchange rates indicates that Iran's economy is out of policymakers' control. Gilani warned that economic pressure and political developments could bring the Islamic Republic closer to collapse.

An image of Gholamreza Jalali, head of the Passive Defense Organization, wearing a smartwatch with location tracking capabilities has been published. This image has sparked ironic reactions because he previously considered smart devices to be security risks. Mehdi Sarami Far described this as an example of managerial inefficiency in the Passive Defense Organization.

Flooding on the afternoon of Saturday, October 3, in Alborz province submerged roads and displaced vehicles. Five watershed workers trapped in Bagestan were rescued by Red Crescent forces. Officials urged people to avoid unnecessary travel in mountainous areas due to ongoing rainfall.

Yemen's government forces targeted Houthi positions in Sanaa and Saada early Sunday, October 3. Intense clashes continue in western Taiz, with around 200,000 displaced people reported. Yemen's Ministry of Defense has launched a general mobilization campaign.

Kayhan newspaper accused a group of using negotiations as a cover for surrender and asking people to submit instead of supporting the country. The newspaper also accused this group of blaming their own country instead of demanding accountability from the war initiator. Kayhan justifies conceding to the aggressor under the name of rationality and expediency.

The Secretary-General of the Nurses' House stated that efforts to secure nurses' rights have been fruitless, and many nurses consider leaving the profession due to low salaries. The average salary of nurses is about 25 to 28 million tomans, equivalent to 100 dollars. He also mentioned the damages caused by inadequate nursing services in hospitals.

Shahram Khaledi stated that the US can limit the presence of Islamic Republic representatives at UN meetings. He said if they stay beyond the allowed time, the US can expel them. This action is viewed as part of diplomatic pressure on the Islamic Republic.

Abbas Golrou announced that the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission is reviewing the simultaneous naval and aerial blockade of Iran. He stated that the Islamic Republic has the necessary tools to counter this. Golrou emphasized that issues should be handled prudently, especially regarding the cancellation of Iran's flights by regional countries.

Nazli Sedghi, a lawyer, warned about the demolition of parts of Rajaee Shahr prison and called for independent investigations. She emphasized that the site should be preserved as its documents and physical space are part of human rights violation cases. Preserving this prison is also essential for safeguarding historical memory and transitional justice.

A group of Iranians living in Calgary, Canada, held a rally for the 40th consecutive week in support of the people of Iran, political prisoners, and Reza Pahlavi. The organizers stated their goal is to convey the voice of the Iranian people to Canadian media and politicians. They announced that these rallies will continue until Iran is free.

Kambiz Tavana from Iran International said that talks of reaching an agreement with the Islamic Republic have decreased, while economic and diplomatic pressure from the US continues. The US military presence in the region has increased. He suggested that if the US engages in conflict, it may adopt a different approach than before.

Videos published on social media show moments of flooding in the streets of Azimieh neighborhood in Karaj on Saturday, October 3. These images depict the condition of the streets during the flood. Reports specify the exact date of the incident.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that the US recently made proposals through a mediator. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened until seven conditions based on the Islamabad agreement are met. Ghalibaf also pointed to increased military threats and cognitive warfare by the enemy.
A young woman in Tehran was set on fire by her husband and died from severe burns. The husband fled the scene and is being pursued by the police.

The Nagoya Asian Games concluded with Japan setting a new record by winning 83 gold medals. Despite Japan's success, there were shortcomings in hosting the event. Somayeh Mehri, a reporter from Iran International, highlighted these issues.

Supporters of the regime chanted slogans against officials at Ali Khamenei's grave. They shouted slogans such as "Turning to inflation, they should compromise with the enemy" and "Economic corruptor, American soldier." The gathering took place at Ali Khamenei's grave.

The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games ended today. Iran became the champion by winning 19 gold medals in sports such as wrestling, taekwondo, and volleyball. The host Japan also set a new record in the number of medals.

A citizen in Jahrom sent a video showing unhealthy and contaminated tap water. He states that after several hours of water outage, the water is now unusable. This issue was reported by Iran International.

Mehdi Chamran stated that he witnessed the moment of the attack on Ali Khamenei's office from the sixth floor of the council building. He added that after seeing smoke and dust, they were informed about the attack and Khamenei's death.
A video has been released showing a fire in shopping centers in Asaluyeh. Witnesses report that the Khalij Fars and Pardis malls caught fire. This incident occurred on Sunday, October 4.

Allahyar Sayyadmanesh was injured in training with Lech Poznań and will be out for about four weeks. During this time, he will miss 9 matches, including three European games. Sayyadmanesh has scored 7 goals and provided 2 assists this season.

Reza Mostafaei, a 26-year-old disabled citizen from Dehdasht, was arrested after appearing at the sixth investigative branch of the prosecutor's office in Kohgiluyeh County and transferred to Dehdasht prison. He had been summoned on charges of propaganda against the regime. His arrest was due to inability to provide an eight billion toman bail.

Esmaeil Baqaei stated that the US proposals on the nuclear issue remain the same as before, and Iran's focus is on the security of the Strait of Hormuz. He also denied reports about Iran agreeing to the return of IAEA inspectors. Iran has communicated its conditions through a seven-day plan to intermediaries.

A video shows a protester in Babolsar writing slogans "Long live the Shah" and "Pahlavi will return" on public pathways. The video was received by Iran International. This act occurred during protests.

Alireza Salimi, Tehran representative, stated that the parliament has a law on 60% enrichment and it cannot be changed by diplomatic talks. The plan to exit the NPT will also be reviewed by the parliament. He mentioned that China did not pay attention to the US requests regarding Iran during the US-China presidential meeting.

Rouhollah Rahimpour referred to Trump's remarks and said more than 100 days have passed since an agreement intended to facilitate nuclear negotiations within 60 days. He added that the Islamic Republic can keep the path to agreement open by accepting verifiable commitments. Otherwise, the US will target missile programs and proxy forces, potentially leading to a widespread war.

Ten students of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad received disciplinary sentences due to their participation in the December 2025 protests. The sentences include one expulsion, eight temporary suspensions totaling 16 semesters, and one written reprimand. The names of these students have been announced.

The Indian captain of the Flydubai flight described the attack by the Omani co-pilot. The co-pilot suddenly attacked him and inflicted severe blows, causing him to nearly lose his sight. The captain managed to open the cabin door to allow passengers to restrain the co-pilot.

Mehdi Kuchakzadeh, a Tehran representative, criticized the Central Bank's approach to the exchange rate, calling it a crime. He objected to the sale of $10,000 to individuals, saying the money benefits the wealthy rather than the people. Kuchakzadeh also expressed concern about the country's situation and its lack of proper governance.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin referred to Qalibaf's remarks, stating that the Islamic Republic has failed with the policies of 'neither war nor negotiation' and 'both war and negotiation.' He described these policies as failed slogans. Akbarin emphasized that the only remaining way is to provide conditions for a normal life.

Merchants of Jannat Bazaar in Tehran protested in front of the City Council due to the failure to move to a new location and officials' neglect. The Jannat Bazaar caught fire in February of last year. The merchants are still waiting to be relocated to the new site.

A group of Iranians living in Germany protested against the Islamic Republic on Saturday, October 3, in the cities of Nuremberg and Hamburg. Videos of these gatherings have been sent to Iran International.

Reza Koushki Nejad, a resident of Lorestan, was summoned to the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Poldokhtar. He is required to appear on Monday, October 12, 2026, to defend against the charge of propaganda against the Islamic Republic system. This summons was issued based on a notification dated October 3, 2026.
The body of a newborn was found on the Siranband road near Buin Bridge in Baneh county. The identity of the newborn and the cause of death have not been determined yet. Investigations are ongoing.

Mohammad Akraminia, the army spokesperson, stated that the Islamic Republic Army intends to increase the speed and range of its missiles. He described the missiles used during the war as very good and said the enemy is located up to a thousand kilometers from Iran's coasts. He also added that good progress has been made in missile speed and targeting accuracy.

Ali Khazarian described the excessive presence of the foreign minister in New York as creating a weak image of Iran. He called the diplomacy of the New York trip undignified and unwise. He also described the Strait of Hormuz as a key point in the global economy and a battlefield.

Mehdi Taj stated that Iran's football quota for next year is 1+3, but club results are not good and teams are deprived of home games. He mentioned the hosting problems of Esteghlal in Iraq and said these issues depend on the country's conditions. Taj also expressed concern about the impact of Russian spectators and referees on the fairness of matches.

The Instagram page of the youth league has published a video showing the latest status of the Azadi Stadium reconstruction. The groundwork and renovation of the stadium's grass are underway. This news was reported by Iran International.
